notes: Identity verified from canonical full-paper text: title I Am What I Do, Not What I Have: The Differential Centrality of Experiential and Material Purchases to the Self; Travis J. Carter and Thomas Gilovich; Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 102(6), 1304–1317 (2012); DOI 10.1037/a0027407. This is the original primary journal report, not a secondary summary or preregistration. No PDF path supplied; no rendering performed. Target identified by Study 3A and the true-self insight question, not by row order or numeric matching. Critical test is the one-sample test of the Person E versus Person M insight rating against the scale midpoint, rather than the adjacent majority z test, purchase-satisfaction paired t test, gender comparison, or correlation. The study identifies 121 participants and scores all responses for the insight measure; no exclusion is reported for that measure. Footnote 4 limits three noncodable purchase-cost responses to the cost comparison and states subsequent results do not change with their inclusion/exclusion. N=121 is the explicitly described participant cohort used in the target analysis, not a df-derived N or sum. Canonical text has systematic symbol substitutions: ! for equals, double quote for less-than, $ for greater-than. Preserve literal text in evidence; p is recorded as the printed less-than .001 bound. d=0.371 is printed directly, with no conversion. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
